Free-trial register — one trial per machine

The free minute is granted at sign-up to the machine named in that sign-up, and a machine already listed here is refused a second one — that is the whole defence against opening new accounts on the same computer to collect the trial again. So when someone signs up on a machine in this list and arrives with nothing in their video bucket, the answer is on this row, not in a bug.

Online payments

Every order the buy page opened — by card or by mobile money — lands here. A customer reaches that page from the Buy button in the app and from your Stream Live page; you never have to send anybody an address. credited means the money arrived and the minutes are already in that account: there is nothing to approve and pressing anything else would pay the customer twice. paid · minutes owed is the one state that needs you: Paystack has the money and the customer has no minutes. Anything else is money that has not become minutes yet, and the last column says why. An order nobody has paid stops waiting by itself after half an hour: it is marked no payment arrived, leaves the "needs attention" list and nothing was ever charged. If that customer's mobile money confirmation still turns up late, the minutes go in by themselves — so never add them a second time by hand.

When the two records disagree, Ask Paystack settles it: it re-asks about that order and puts the minutes in if the money is there. Pressing it twice cannot pay anybody twice — an order already credited answers "already credited earlier". The line above the list says whether Paystack has an address to call when a payment finishes; that address is how the app hears about a payment by itself, without anybody keeping a page open.

Key pool

For every call the gateway tries the key assigned to that account first, then every enabled key by ascending priority, skipping any that already hit its daily cap, and only then the env secret. A key that fails is logged and the next one is tried in the same request, so one bad key never takes the product down. Users never see, send or store any of this.

Add a key pair

Paste each provider's key and press Verify — that asks the provider itself, right now, without billing a single second of inference. When every box you filled turns green, save. DeCart trial keys have their own tab; a row stored here can still carry one, and its tail shows in the table below so nothing is hidden.

DeCart keys — the free-trial supply

Add as many as you like. Every brand new account's free 1 minute of video is served from this list, and only from this list, so trial traffic never puts a cent of charge on your fal.ai account.

The gateway works down this table in priority order: a key that is disabled, that has already spent its trial-minute budget, or that hit its daily cap is skipped and the next one is tried inside the same call. Only when no key here can serve does a trial account get "lines are busy" — the trial is refused, never billed to fal.

Rough sizing: 1 DeCart key ≈ 1,000 credits ≈ 8 minutes of video ≈ 8 free trials. Type that 8 into the budget when you link a fresh key and the panel will tell you when it runs dry.

Trial capacity right now

The gateway's own count, not arithmetic done on this page. A minute a customer stopped streaming early goes back into the key it came from, so this figure tracks what DeCart actually owes you.

Add a DeCart key

Get it from decart.ai → dashboard → API keys. Press Verify first: that asks DeCart for a short call token — a handshake, not a generation, so it costs no credits. Save it only when the box turns green.

Which video service answers a call

Two suppliers, one product. The customer sees the same Start button either way and never learns which one served them.

Trial poolDeCart · Lucy 2.5

Serves every brand new account and nothing else: the free 1 minute of video, video only, once per account, for as long as that account has never been credited or bought a minute. A trial minute burns at 1x, so the minute you promise is the minute they stream.

Paid servicefal.ai · LUCY 2.5 realtime

Serves anyone who has ever had minutes credited or bought, plus every voice call. That switch is permanent in both directions of bookkeeping: an account that paid once is never moved back to the trial pool, even if its balance later reaches zero.

When the trial pool has no key left, a trial account is told the lines are busy and nothing is billed to fal.ai. That refusal is the protection on your fal balance — turning on the fallback below removes it.

Where the trial supply comes from

DeCart keys, their budgets and the live capacity count all live on the DeCart keys tab. Nothing here needs to know how many keys you have.

Free trial switches

Same config row the gateway reads on every call start. Nothing here is visible to a customer.

Video bucket only. A new account gets this the moment it is created, so the Minutes page already reads the trial before they press Start. Existing accounts are not topped up.
0 or blank = no limit. The third caller is told "lines are busy" instead of burning a lease and failing.
Off = nobody is ever granted a trial minute, every account behaves exactly as it did before, and no DeCart key is used. Switch it on when the pool is linked and verified.
Costs you money. Every free trial then bills fal.ai at the paid rate. Leave this off unless you have decided to pay for that.

Every account, split by the video service that serves it

Left is the trial pool (DeCart): accounts that have only ever had their free minute. Right is the paid service (fal.ai): anyone who has been credited or bought a real amount of minutes, plus anything you pin there.

Crossing to the paid side is permanent — crediting one real minute moves an account across for good, even if its balance later falls to zero, so an account never drifts back onto the trial keys. This list is the same decision the gateway makes when a call starts; it is computed here, not stored, so it cannot go stale.

Served by is a switch you can throw. Automatic lets the normal rule decide; Paid service or Trial pool pins that one account. A pin holds until you put the account back on Automatic — with one exception: pinning an already-credited account to the trial pool has no effect, because real minutes always mean the paid service.

The cedi rate every price is converted at

Your packages are priced in dollars. The buyer is charged in cedis: each dollar price is multiplied by this figure at the moment their order is opened. Change it here when the rate moves and every Buy button in the app and every price on the checkout page follow it at once — no package has to be re-typed.

Packages you sell

One line per package: what the buyer pays, the minutes they get, what those minutes cost you in AI time, and how many accounts hold it. Edit opens that package so you can change it and see it exactly as the buyer does; the switch in the "On sale" column puts a package on the buyer's screen or takes it off, immediately, without opening anything.

Payment and contact details shown to users

MoMo and Bitcoin are the only two methods the desktop app advertises, and WhatsApp and Telegram are the only two contact centres it links to. Everything here appears on the user's Plans screen and Minutes page with a copy button beside each value. Empty fields stay hidden.

Set your prices in three steps

Step 1 says what the AI services charge you. Step 2 says how much of each sale you want to keep. Step 3 writes the price for any package you like. Nothing here goes on sale — every package created here starts switched off, and you turn it on in the Plans tab.

Why a minute you sell costs less than a minute of airtime

A minute you sell is what leaves the buyer's balance. A minute of airtime is what the AI services bill you for. The burn rate you set on the Burn rates tab decides how many sold minutes fit into one airtime minute, and that is the only reason the two numbers differ — change the burn rate and every figure on this page changes with it.

So a sale pays you twice. The buyer's cash minus the airtime they actually used is your first pocket. The minutes they were sold but never burned stay on your AI account and are never charged against you — that is the second pocket, and it is why a customer who buys 10 minutes and uses 7.7 leaves you with more than the cash difference.

Every figure here is the AI bill alone — hosting, MoMo fees and your own time are not in it.
